extracted.intended_audience: CIHR peer reviewers and applicants to the CIHR Project Grant competition (review committee members and prospective applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric and procedures for peer review of CIHR Project Grant applications, specifying the adjudication criteria, weights, review process (internal scoring + committee discussion), DORA-aligned assessment of outputs, and scoring thresholds used to make funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept (60% weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the proposed research. CIHR lists Concept as one of two adjudication criteria and assigns it 60% of the overall weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate: Importance of the research question; Originality of the approach; Significance of expected outcomes; Theoretical framework soundness; Use of preliminary data to support feasibility. This criterion is the majority determinant of application quality (60% weight). Consider how well the research question is posed, how novel the approach is, and whether preliminary data justify the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (40% weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood of success. CIHR lists Feasibility as the second adjudication criterion and assigns it 40% of the overall weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate: Methods appropriate to the question; Approach rigor; Team expertise and capacity; Resources sufficient; Timeline realistic; Risk mitigation plan. Focus on whether the proposed methods and team can realistically deliver the proposed outcomes within resources and timeline (40% weight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale and funding threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scale used by reviewers to rate criteria and guide funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 0–4.9 indicates does not meet criterion (low quality). Ranges include 3.0–3.5 = competent but limited; 3.5–4.0 = strong; 4.0–4.5 = excellent; 4.5–5.0 = exceptional. A combined score of >= 4.0 is typically required for funding. Reviewers provide pre-meeting individual scores and committees arrive at final consensus scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA-aligned assessment of research outputs and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practices for evaluating applicant productivity and outputs consistent with DORA (Declaration on Research Assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are instructed NOT to use Journal Impact Factor as a proxy for quality. Applicants are asked to explain the context and significance of selected publications. Reviewers evaluate up to 5 most significant publications rather than citation totals. Diverse research outputs (datasets, software, policy papers) are counted as evidence of productivity. Evaluate the significance and context of selected outputs rather than relying on journal metrics or publication counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tier review structure (internal review + committee discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural structure for how applications are reviewed and how scores are produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1 — Internal Peer Review: Each application assigned 4 internal reviewers (members of the Peer Review Committee) who score Concept and Feasibility with pre-meeting individual scoring. Tier 2 — Committee Discussion: The Peer Review Committee meets virtually to discuss each application and assign final consensus scores. Use pre-meeting scores to inform but not replace committee deliberation; consensus scoring finalizes rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias mitigation and reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR requires reviewer training and bias-mitigation practices as part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR trained reviewers on bias mitigation following evidence (Witteman 2019) pointing to gender gaps. This includes operational reforms (e.g., DORA adoption) and instruction to avoid inappropriate proxies (like JIF). Reviewers should apply equitable assessment practices and be aware of systemic biases when evaluating applicants and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI-focused evaluation (historical Foundation Grants criteria — discontinued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria historically used in CIHR's Foundation Grants program to evaluate the applicant (PI) rather than primarily the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically reviewers were asked to focus on PI's calibre / track record, research vision, and PI productivity. Empirical evidence (Witteman 2019) showed larger gender gaps under this model; CIHR discontinued the Foundation Grant in its prior form and consolidated toward Project Grant criteria to reduce bias. This historical criterion serves as a cautionary example of PI-focused assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit weighting of adjudication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Design principle that the two adjudication criteria (Concept and Feasibility) have explicit numeric weights (60/40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR uses explicit weighting (Concept 60%, Feasibility 40%) as a transparency mechanism compared with funders that use holistic Overall Impact scores. Rubric designers should consider clear weights to communicate the relative importance of dimensions to reviewers and applicants.
